subject: Unusual API traffic — request for IR plan, SOC 2 / SIG evidence and escalation
messages:
From: Alex Romero <alex.romero@greenlinefin.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Patel <s.patel@greenlinefin.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 08:12:14 -0700
Subject: Unusual API traffic — request for IR plan, SOC 2 / SIG evidence and escalation

Hi Sean,

We're seeing an elevated rate of 401/429 spike against our integrations with Redwood between 02:43 - 02:55 UTC this morning (approx). A sample request id set is attached (auth-telemetry-sample-ids.txt). We haven't been able to map it to scheduled jobs on our side.

Can you please:
- Confirm whether this looks like targeted credential stuffing or a gateway misconfiguration on Redwood's side
- Share your incident response plan summary and the SOC 2 / SIG/CAIQ artifacts that map to authentication and logging controls (we need these for our audit and to brief our security ops)
- Escalate to the appropriate on-call/contact for faster triage — we may need a bridged troubleshooting session in the next 2 hours

We're under a compliance window for an internal audit and need an interim evidence snapshot (redacted fine) showing:
1) authentication failure logs for the window
2) timeline of any service-side deploys or config changes
3) contact for escalation / on-call rota

I can share a presigned S3 link for our telemetry if you prefer a secure pull.

Thanks — apologizing for the urgency.

Alex Romero
Lead Platform Security, Greenline Financial
alex.romero@greenlinefin.com
+1 415-555-0142

Attachment: auth-telemetry-sample-ids.txt (text, 2 KB)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@greenlinefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 08:37:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual API traffic — request for IR plan, SOC 2 / SIG evidence and escalation

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the sample IDs. We appreciate the detail.

Immediate plan from our side (next 90 minutes):
- I've looped in Marissa (security ops) and Ben (forensics) for a focused collection.
- Marissa: please generate a redacted evidence snapshot (auth failure logs, token validation traces) for 02:30 - 03:00 UTC and upload to the secure evidence bucket. Include any deploy/change metadata.
- Ben: run KV cache and rate-limit traces for the same window; flag any anomalous user-agent strings.
- I'll coordinate a 30-min bridge at 09:15 PT. If 09:15 doesn't work we can move earlier.

For Greenline audit asks: we can provide the following artifacts quickly (redacted):
- IR playbook excerpt (authentication & rate-limiting runbook) — pdf
- SOC 2 control mapping for CC6 (logical access) and CC7 (system logging) — SIG/CAIQ crosswalk spreadsheet
- Sample telemetry extracts (redacted request ids, timestamps, headers) as a zipped archive

Preferred transfer method: we can receive your presigned S3 link and place our collected artifacts in a locked folder with short TTL, or we can push the artifacts to your secure SharePoint if you prefer.

Can you confirm the presigned link or preferred transfer and who from your side will join the bridge? Also confirm whether Greenline requires evidence mapped to auditor control IDs (e.g., SOC2 — CC6.1/CC6.2).

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Security Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

--

Sean / Alex — I'm on it. Quick status and asks: 

Status (T+30m):
- I've started a scoped collection for 02:30 - 03:05 UTC and will redact PII before sharing.
- No active deploy in our control plane in that window per the deploy ledger (checked).
- Initial telemetry suggests a surge of token validation errors from a small set of IPs; I'm exporting UA strings and rate-limit counters now.

What we'll produce by EOB (or sooner if triage requires):
- ir_playbook_v3.pdf (authentication section excerpt) — highlights RTO/RPO and escalation matrix
- sig-caiq-mapping.xlsx — mapping of SIG controls to our evidence artifacts (auth, logging, monitoring)
- auth-telemetry-sample-ids.txt (redacted) and a zipped telemetry extract (redwood_auth_telemetry_20260930.zip)
- short timeline.txt with our annotated events and internal tickets

Questions for Greenline:
1) For evidence redaction, do you prefer request id -> hashed id mapping, or we should remove headers entirely?
2) Please confirm who from your side will accept the evidence (name + email) and whether we should use your S3 link or an internal secure transfer.

Ben/ Karthik: please include the forensic notes and a suggested summary suitable for SOC 2 auditor consumption (one-page control mapping).

Alex: happy to join the bridge at 09:15 PT. If you want earlier, propose a slot and I'll try to pull the team.

-Marissa
Director, Security Operations
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa / Sean — appreciate the quick triage.

Per your questions:
- Redaction: please map request-id -> stable-hash (sha256 prefix ok) and remove any customer PII fields. Hash will allow cross-correlation with our side without exposing raw identifiers.
- Evidence acceptor: Sarah Patel (s.patel@greenlinefin.com). We'll accept a short-lived S3 folder (48 hour TTL) containing the zipped artifacts.

I've uploaded a presigned PUT-enabled S3 path for you: https://glf-secure.s3.amazonaws.com/presigned/triage-20260930 (expires 2026-10-03). Use the secure-submission instructions in the doc below for naming conventions.

Outstanding asks for SOC2 mapping: our auditor needs mapping specifically to CC6.1, CC6.2 (authentication) and CC7.3 (system monitoring). If possible, include the auditor-oriented one-page control mapping Ben mentioned.

We'll join the bridge for a 09:15 PT slot tomorrow (I assume you meant 09:15 PT on the 1st). Please send a calendar invite with a dial-in.

Alex Romero
Lead Platform Security, Greenline Financial
